title: Live timeline follow-ups from the RF-188 review
acceptance: On short phones the More panel (which holds the timeline) does not collapse after every timeline release that briefly makes music wait; it still collapses for a real playback failure, or the record states why the collapse is kept.

Done in #738 round 3: a system pointercancel or lost capture during a press that never moved commits nothing and puts the clock back where it was before the press (kept here as the record of that review finding).
The timeline hint also tells keyboard users how to move (for example "Arrow keys to nudge"), or the record states why All tracks is enough.

apps/web/src/lib/trailing-throttle.ts and its test, and the run-generation bookkeeping in lib/playback/runtime.ts (getRunGeneration), all unused since RF-188, are removed, with the RF-108 and RF-185 source evidence that cites them retargeted so pnpm tasks:check still passes.

Owner device check: whether tap to jump feels right on a real iPhone. A tap that moves more than 3 px commits an exact time instead of the track start, and grabbing the playhead mid-track to nudge it restarts the track if the finger lifts within 3 px (Air final review finding 5).

While a finger is held on the strip, the runtime transport sampling cannot auto-advance to the next track and then have the release seek enter again (Air final review finding 4; it already happened under the old throttle), or the record states why one extra entry at a track boundary is acceptable.

The Live timeline callout and the Live header name the same track in a free-timeline gap: LiveTimeline blockAt and runtime segmentAt / LiveMode trackIndexAt share one rule (Air round-2 review finding 7).
LiveMode passes no separate onSeekRelease when it equals onSeekCommit (seekRelease is a pure alias of seek), or the record states why the alias is kept (finding 8).

Scrub state does not re-render the whole Live tree twice per tap (for example a ref plus a small store read only by the rail and the recovery panel), or the record states why two renders per tap are acceptable (finding 9).

Owner decision recorded (RF-188 round 3-4 watchdog): after 10 s with no pointer event the host clock and position sync resume while the finger stays down, but the coordinator is not ticked until the finger lifts (round 4), so a still hold in a silence gap no longer starts the provider twice; instead the resumed clock stops at the gap end until the lift. In music mode the clock and callout follow the audio until the lift, and the watchdog moment can briefly show the uncommitted tap target. In prompter-only mode an unmoved press that is cancelled restores the clock to its pre-press time, losing the hold duration, and unmounting the strip mid-press keeps the previewed time. Keep, or change the watchdog.

A new press that drops a stale gesture reads its pre-press clock from the last committed position, not the stale gesture uncommitted preview, so an unmoved cancel of the new press restores a real position (Air round-3 review finding 4).
The All tracks button is hidden or does nothing confusing while the Full List view is already showing (finding 8).

If no end event ever reaches the strip or the window, "Seeking…" and the quiet waiting panel last until the next touch on the strip (finger-down has no cap since round 4; a real failure still shows); decide whether to end such a gesture as a lost release after a longer timeout (for example twice the watchdog), against the owner rule that the watchdog must not drop the gesture.
